active_questions.q: Which regulatory circuits exhibit bistability or switch-like behaviour, and what evidence establishes the switch rather than a graded response?
active_questions._acquisition_note: First-pass swept 2026-08-09. 'Switch' is a heavily overloaded word: false positives from immunology (antibody class-switch recombination), chemistry, and optogenetics appear interleaved with genuine bistability content rather than cleanly separated (unlike glmp-q3's recovery-then-off pattern). 5-point percentile-block title reading found the on-topic majority ends around p27/p28 and never clearly regains it. Cutoff 0.375 -> 1,241 papers (963 new, 278 merged). One paper (pubmed_19910671) legitimately qualifies for both glmp-q3 and glmp-q4.

active_questions.q: What synthetic gene circuits have been built and characterised, and how does their designed logic compare to natural circuits?
active_questions._acquisition_note: First-pass swept 2026-08-09 (the pilot question for this whole expansion, GLMP_MASTER_TODO.md item 53) -- backfilled into this file 2026-08-13 after a full-suite audit found it missing here despite being live in Firestore all along; a bookkeeping gap, not a missing sweep. 7,561 unique PMIDs. Decile scores were smooth with no visible cliff; falloff found by reading titles instead -- unambiguous through ~p48 (score ~0.36), a hard qualitative turn by the mid-50s (melanoma classifiers, neural stimulators, oxytocin receptor comparisons) despite continuous-looking scores.
